title: And I Serve: Biplane pilot (no lower thirds)
description: When Senior Airman Phil Owens isn't working as a crew chief in the 192nd Aircraft Maintenance Squadron, he's flying tours of Acadia National Park in Maine. Just two weeks after starting this, his first commercial flying job, he experienced catastrophic engine failure and had to perform and emergency off-airport landing. Owens tells his story in this edition of "And I Serve". No lower thirds.

transcript.text: - I'm Phil Owens and I fly aerial tours
of Acadia Park in Maine.
(upbeat music)
(airplane engine roaring)
And I serve.
I'm a crew chief in the Virginia Air National Guard.
I'm responsible for ensuring safe operations
of all systems on the F-22 Raptor.
The Guard is part time and that works well for me
cause I love flying this plane.
So a tour pilot, we greet 'em at the front gate,
we load 'em up in the plane,
take 'em for a ride just around Bar Harbor, Maine
and around Acadia National Park here.
This is my first commercial flying job.
I joined the Air National Guard at 17,
did drills throughout my senior year of high school,
then after tech school,
I used my education benefits to get a aviation degree,
as well as my commercial pilots license.
(radio transmission of distress call)
- We had seconds to make decisions
and they had to be good decisions.
- Well, we're flying over here in Maine,
you got a lot of water and a lot of national parks,
so not too many good landing spots
in the case of an engine failure,
but I was able to find a swamp or marsh
kind of flared as much as I could to keep
that air speed low
and so it wasn't too abrupt of an impact,
but you definitely felt it in your seat there.
The type of aircraft I fly here is a
tailwheel or taildragger,
so that two wheels are upfront
and so once those kind of finally set down in that marsh,
the aircraft flipped over on to that top wing there.
So after we flipped over,
course I unbuckled there
and kind of checked on the passengers up front of me.
There were two passengers that day.
Looked at both of them
and didn't see any blood or major injuries.
And they both told me they were okay.
- He had very little time in the biplane when this happened.
And he was steady.
He was cool.
Couldn't a done a better job if you woulda had too.
Did a great job.
- Kinda told the passengers to hold on
and I'd get 'em down safely
and grateful I did.
I'm Senior A Phil Owens and I am the VaANG.
(wind rushing)
(engine roaring)
(instrumental music)
